keyFacts: Native checkboxes look different in every browser and OS, which is why designers restyle them with CSS.
The standard technique keeps the real input in the DOM (visually hidden) and styles a sibling element, preserving keyboard and screen-reader support.
The :checked pseudo-class combined with the adjacent-sibling selector (+) is what flips the styled box between states.
The checkmark is drawn with a rotated bordered box via ::after — no image or icon font needed.
Switches are the same idea with a wider track and a sliding knob moved by translateX.
A visible :focus-visible outline is essential so keyboard users can see which control is active.
